newsitem.title: UK: UK builders could take unofficial strike action.
newsitem.headline: UK builders could take unofficial strike action.

text.p: British building workers could take unofficial strike action in a dispute over pay, threatening high profile construction projects such as the London Underground's Jubilee Line and the Millennium Dome, union officials said on Thursday.

The GMB and Transport and General Workers unions will be balloted next Wednesday on official action, but union representatives said anger over a pay freeze since talks with employers collapsed at the end of May could mean a spontaneous strike.
GMB national officer Allan Black told a news conference, "There is a chance building workers could go on strike unofficially." But he said the union would not want to encourage this.

The union members will be balloted on the same day that British Airways Plc cabin crew are set to start a series of 72 hour stoppages over pay. BA said on Thursday it had sent a proposal to arbitration service ACAS to try and settle the dispute.

Construction workers have not gone on strike since 1973, but the dispute with the Construction Confederation flared up after the Confederation withdrew a three-year pay deal, which the unions rejected as unrealistic.
"There are skill shortages, things are improving," T&G national officer George Henderson said. "Not enough money is being offered."
The unions are confident of getting strong backing for a strike when results of the ballot are published on July 25.

Black said if members backed industrial action an indefinite strike would be called from August 5, aiming to cause maximum disruption to employers, including Tarmac Plc, Costain Group Plc, John Laing Plc and George Wimpey Plc.
